core_obligations: Use the Noetherian pseudo-coherence statement to conclude that tau_{<= m}K is pseudo-coherent for all m, hence represented by a bounded above complex P^bullet of finite free A-modules (proof lines 27275-27278).

Compute tau_{<= m}K tensor^L_A A/I^n = P^bullet/I^nP^bullet and conclude that the derived completion of tau_{<= m}K is R lim P^bullet/I^nP^bullet, quoting the Noetherian naive-completion proposition (proof lines 27279-27281).

Use that the R lim is termwise lim and that I-adic completion is exact on finite A-modules, quoting the computation and Algebra statements, to conclude the result for tau_{<= m}K (proof lines 27282-27286).
Conclude the result for K since derived completion has finite cohomological dimension (proof lines 27286-27288).
difficulty_reason: Let A be a Noetherian ring and I an ideal. The lemma takes an object K of D(A) whose cohomology modules H^n(K) are finite for all n, and asserts that the cohomology modules H^n(K^wedge) of the derived completion are the I-adic completions of the cohomology modules H^n(K) (source lines 27265-27272). The proof works by truncation. For every m the complex tau_{<= m}K is pseudo-coherent by the Noetherian pseudo-coherence statement, hence represented by a bounded above complex P^bullet of finite free A-modules (proof lines 27275-27278). Then tau_{<= m}K tensor^L_A A/I^n = P^bullet/I^nP^bullet, so the derived completion of tau_{<= m}K is R lim P^bullet/I^nP^bullet, by the Noetherian naive-completion proposition (proof lines 27279-27281). Since that R lim is computed termwise by the computation statement, and since I-adic completion is exact on finite A-modules by the Algebra flatness statement, the result holds for tau_{<= m}K (proof lines 27282-27286). The result for K then follows because derived completion has finite cohomological dimension (proof lines 27286-27288). The non-routine content is the reduction to bounded-above truncations: it converts a statement about an arbitrary K into a statement about a bounded above complex of finite free modules, where the termwise R lim and exactness of completion can be applied.
